newsitem.title: ALBANIA: U.S. suspends Albania airlift, Germans open fire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. suspends Albania airlift, Germans open fire.

text.p: The United States suspended the evacuation of its citizens from anarchic Albania on Friday after two helicopters came under fire, while German troops exchanged fire with gunmen during their own rescue mission.

The Pentagon said an SA-7 shoulder-launched missile was fired at a Marine Cobra helicopter and another Cobra came under small arms attack and returned the fire. But all helicopters involved in the operation returned to their ships.

Germany sent five military helicopters to rescue 105 of its nationals and other Europeans, but one Albanian was injured when German troops traded fire with unidentified local gunmen who shot at the evacuees and the aircraft.
Earlier on Friday, an Italian military helicopter involved in the airlift was hit by small arms fire over Tirana, but no-one was hurt.
The curfew was brought forward by one hour to 7 p.m. and one police officer said he had orders to shoot at anyone on the streets after that time.
In Tirana, political leaders made repeated attempts to calm the anarchy that has broken out in the past 48 hours as looters loosed off bursts of automatic weapons fire.
European envoy Franz Vranitzky held talks with Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and rebel leaders aboard the Italian frigate Aliseo in the Adriatic.

Vranitzky, who represents the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, said he would urge the European Union and OSCE member states to give serious thought to a request from Tirana to send in military support to Albania.
He told Reuters by telephone from the Aliseo he believed order could only be restored in Albania with outside help.

Officials at a military hospital in the Albanian capital said four people were killed and 72 injured by stray bullets overnight. Local media said more than 100 people had died since the unrest erupted earlier this month.
In further evidence of growing lawlessness, one man carrying a rifle was gunned down in daylight in a Tirana street by four men who drove by in a van, witnesses said.

Later, two armoured personnel carriers and a convoy of vans full of armed men paraded along the capital's main street in an apparent show of strength which coincided with an announcement that police pay had been upped by 300 percent.
Giant Chinook military helicopters plucked about 100 Italians from Tirana's football stadium soon after dawn on Friday, completing an Italian evacuation of about 1,000 of its nationals.

American Sea Knight and Sea Stallion helicopters flew from U.S. Navy amphibious ships in the Adriatic to rescue up to 2,200 Americans from the embassy housing complex in Tirana, while Cobra escort helicopters circled overhead.
U.S. officials said 408 Americans were evacuated from Tirana before the suspension and about 150 Marines remained in Albania. The suspension would last at least several hours.
As the Americans flew out, U.S. ambassador Marisa Lino appeared on Albanian television to assure Albanians that the United States was not abandoning them.
"The United States of America is not leaving Albania," she said. "I and some of my team will remain."
France sent four helicopters to Albania on Friday to evacuate 100 French nationals and those of several other countries from the port of Durres.
Britain said it had evacuated 131 people from Albania on Friday morning and they were on their way to the Italian Adriatic Sea port of Brindisi in an Italian naval ship.
The Greek frigate "Kavaloudis" evacuated 49 people -- 44 Greeks and five Belgians -- from the Albanian port of Durres, west of Tirana, on Friday, defence ministry officials said.

At least 14 Albanian navy craft, most of them small patrol boats built nearly 50 years ago by the Chinese, limped into southern Italian ports under Italian navy escort after crossing the southern Adriatic with deserting servicemen and civilians.
Former Albanian Defence Minister Safet Zhulali and his family arrived in Italy on a merchant ship on Friday with about 70 other people fleeing the chaos in their homeland.
Albania's revolt, which began in the south where people lost their savings in collapsed pyramid investment schemes, has spread to the north of the country since mid-week.
